title: Two TESS binary records reject an apsidal-motion null with fixed curvature signs after error doubling and each season deletion
abstract: We test full apsidal motion as an alternative to common timing changes in 14 southern binary candidates. We use 672 published TESS eclipse times from 2018 to 2026. For a regular edge-on orbit with fixed eccentricity and a steady apsidal rate, the primary and secondary timing curves have opposite curvature signs while the periapse stays in one curvature interval. We fit a larger convex and concave curve class and compute dual lower bounds on its loss. Seven records reject this class with doubled errors at a conservative Gaussian threshold of 0.05/557. Four retain rejection after every single-event deletion. ASAS J090232-5653.4 and J063202-6750.7 retain rejection after every single-season deletion. A relaxation that permits one curvature reversal is not rejected for any record. Full uniform-apsidal searches with eccentricity caps up to 0.999 find no noise-sized fit, but do not prove global minima. The result supplies a reusable test and strengthens a restricted timing claim for two systems. It adds no observation or third-star detection. Limits include inherited eclipse fits, independent Gaussian errors, the edge-on geometry and fixed-element assumptions, and the no-reversal scope. Code, timing inputs, numerical certificates, fit endpoints and fresh-scratch replay instructions are preserved.

display.caption: Seven full timing records reject fixed opposite curvature signs with doubled errors. Two retain rejection after each season deletion. A one-reversal relaxation passes for all 14. The threshold assumes independent Gaussian errors and uses 557 stars for the family correction.

Primary and secondary timing residuals in the two records that retain rejection after each season deletion. Dashed curves show the best attained full uniform-apsidal fits. Separate affine ephemerides are removed for display. Error bars are original errors with the source floor.

citations.reason: We reuse its derived TESS timing measurements and test the uniform apsidal-motion alternative for its 14 strong common-mode candidates. Support is limited to the stated model and error assumptions.
Earlier separate primary and secondary period tests did not remove all nonlinear apsidal terms.
Earlier quadratic common-drift tests left full apsidal motion open.
